children: The UK's main stock indexes recovered on Thursday as a rally in global bonds ahead of a U.S. jobs report lifted risk sentiment, while firmer commodity prices provided additional support.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
rose 0.1% to 10,767.57 points by 10:10 GMT, while the midcap FTSE 250
gained 0.1%, rebounding from a nearly one-month low.

Britain's 10-year gilt yields (GB10YT=RR) eased more than 29 basis points from an 18-year high of Wednesday, tracking a rally in global bonds and stocks ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
The services sector in the UK grew for the second month in a row in August and confidence rose, a survey showed.
Rate-sensitive banks (.FTNMX301010) rose 0.2%.
Healthcare stocks (.FTUB2010) advanced 0.9% higher, supported by weaker sterling, with AstraZeneca
Precious metal miners
gained 0.9% as gold and silver prices rose.
Telecom stocks Airtel Africa
and Vodafone
rose between 3.3% and 3.8%, leading sectoral gains.
Luxury retailer Burberry
slipped 1.9%, as weak demand prospects weighed on the sector across Europe, sending the broader personal goods sector (.FTNMX402040) down 2.2%, leading sectoral losses.
Hilton Food Group
jumped 16.7%, among the top gainers in the mid-cap index after raising annual profit forecast.
